Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

of preposition

also one of, some of, none of us, made of, a cup of, the house of

classical

Sen. Ep. 58.22: nēmō nostrum
Cato Agr. 158.1: aquae sextāriōs sex
Liv. 21.1.4: annōrum fermē novem

cāsus genetīvus

construction: the genitive case, with no preposition

of (the owner, the whole, the amount, the quality)

Latin has no word for “of”; the genitive does its work: the owner (capillī capitis, the hairs of the head), the whole that a part is taken from (nēmō nostrum, none of us), an amount (aquae sextāriōs sex, six pints of water), and an age or a quality (annōrum novem, nine years old). Not with a name: “the city of Rome” is urbs Rōma, the two nouns in the same case.

Other words

  • ex, ē + abl. — of (one of several; made of)

    preposition with the ablative; ē only before consonants · also used · classical · Liv. 2.13.6: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus; Cic. Verr. 2.2.21: statua ex aere facta (Lewis & Short)

    After a number or ūnus, and for the stuff a thing is made of.

  • dē + abl. — of, from (a part taken off a whole)

    preposition with the ablative · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 158.1: ungulam dē pernā

    A piece taken from something, in plain and kitchen Latin: ungulam dē pernā, a hock off the ham.

  • nōmen adjectīvum (paternus, aureus) — of (my father’s, of gold): an adjective instead of the genitive

    construction: an adjective agreeing with its noun · also used · classical · Hor. C. 2.16.13–14: paternum … salīnum; Sen. Ep. 119.3: aureum pōculum

    Latin likes an adjective for a family member or a material: domus paterna, the family house; pōculum aureum, a cup of gold.

Examples

  • Vestrī autem capillī capitis omnēs numerātī sunt.

    And the very hairs of your head are all numbered.Mt. 10.30

  • nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē

    none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day beforeSen. Ep. 58.22

  • Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … frūstrāta custōdēs, dux agminis virginum inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit

    Cloelia, a girl, one of the hostages, gave her guards the slip and swam the Tiber at the head of a band of girls, under the enemy’s spearsLiv. 2.13.6

  • sūme tibi ōllam, additō eō aquae sextāriōs sex et eō additō ungulam dē pernā

    take a pot, put six pints of water in it, and put in a hock off the hamCato Agr. 158.1

  • Hannibalem annōrum fermē novem, puerīliter blandientem patrī Hamilcarī ut dūcerētur in Hispāniam

    Hannibal, about nine years old, coaxing his father Hamilcar like a little boy to take him to SpainLiv. 21.1.4

  • vīvitur parvō bene, cui paternum splendet in mēnsā tenuī salīnum

    he lives well on little whose father’s salt-cellar shines on a plain tableHor. C. 2.16.13–14

  • utrum sit aureum pōculum an crustallinum an murreum an Tīburtīnus calix an manus concava, nihil rēfert

    whether it is a cup of gold, of crystal or of agate, a mug from Tibur or a cupped hand, makes no differenceSen. Ep. 119.3

  • dē lignō

    (made) out of woodTraupman 355

See also by, one of.
